The guidelines provide a structured approach to developing a comprehensive multi-year plan (cMYP) for immunization, including planning and costing tools. The cMYP is designed to be a dynamic document, periodically updated to adapt to changing conditions, generate evidence-based budget requests, and provide information for advocacy and reporting. While this guide offers one method for creating a multi-year plan, countries with existing planning methods can use the cMYP guidelines and tools to enhance quality and serve as a reference for national program planners. The cMYP focuses on seven key steps: conducting a situation analysis, setting objectives and milestones, planning strategies, linking to national and international goals, creating activity timelines with monitoring and evaluation frameworks, assessing costs and financing gaps, and implementing the plan through detailed annual workplans. The Global Vaccine Action Plan (GVAP), adopted in 2012, serves as a framework to prevent millions of deaths by 2020 through equitable access to vaccines. It builds on the Global Immunization Vision and Strategy (GIVS) and emphasizes sustainable financing, country ownership, and innovation. Countries are expected to report progress annually using a common monitoring and evaluation framework. The GVAP highlights six strategic objectives, including prioritizing immunization, increasing public understanding and demand, ensuring equitable access, strengthening health systems, securing sustainable funding and supply, and fostering research and development. The cMYP guidelines have been updated to reflect advancements in vaccines, immunization technologies, and global health policies. These updates include aligning strategies with the GVAP, emphasizing links between immunization programs and health sector planning, and developing user-friendly costing and financing tools. The guidelines also stress the importance of integrating immunization with other health interventions, such as vitamin A supplementation and malaria prevention, to maximize impact and efficiency. Developing a cMYP involves a sequential process, starting with convening key immunization stakeholders to coordinate and integrate all aspects of the national program into a unified plan. This includes incorporating findings from recent immunization reviews, aligning with national health sector plans, and ensuring that costs and financing are fully accounted for. Stakeholders, including government officials, civil society, and the private sector, play a critical role in advocating for resources, enacting supportive policies, and ensuring high-quality service delivery. The cMYP serves as a vital tool for national immunization programs, enabling them to align with global health targets, secure sustainable financing, and integrate with broader health sector strategies. By fostering collaboration among stakeholders and leveraging synergies with other health interventions, the cMYP supports the achievement of national health goals and the reduction of morbidity and mortality rates.
